title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Buying a Higher Free-Time Product
content:
## Clause

The billed party can purchase a higher Demurrage and Detention Free Time product for a record whose free time has not yet run out. Free time running is the only status in which a purchase can be made; a record already accruing charges is past that point, and no purchase can be given an earlier date than the one on which it is made.

## Conditions on the product bought

Every one of the following must hold, and each is read from the company's records rather than from what the customer says:

- [ ] the product is one that is sold as an upgrade;
- [ ] its rank is higher than the rank of the product the record carries now;
- [ ] the container's rate class is one of the classes the product accepts;
- [ ] fewer upgrades have been bought on this record, counting its whole life, than the upgrade allowance of the product it now carries;
- [ ] the purchase is also permitted under the rule on the customer's overdue demurrage and detention balance.

Upgrades to AHL Contract Free Time 30 are not offered at all.

## Ranking of the range

| Rank | Product |
|---|---|
| 1 | AHL Tariff Free Time |
| 2 | AHL Free Time Extension 3 |
| 3 | AHL Free Time Extension 7 |
| 4 | AHL Combined Free Time 14 |
| 5 | AHL Combined Free Time 21 |
| 6 | AHL Contract Free Time 30 |

## Price

The charge is the difference between the two list prices, the new product's less the current product's, which keeps the customer from paying twice for the same days. The charge is booked to the record's balance as a free-time extension fee.

## Effect

Once bought, the new product replaces the old one on the record, and the clock rules then apply it to all of the record's clocks. An early return of the container brings no refund of a product already bought.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A record on a product listed at 100.00 moves to one listed at 180.00: the charge is 80.00.
- A record already showing charges accruing cannot take any purchase, whatever the product.
- A request to buy a product ranked below, or equal to, the one on the record fails the rank condition.
